name: performance-testing
description: Performance testing — JMeter load plans, thresholds, CI-safe execution
body:
# Performance Testing

Apply when editing JMeter plans, Playwright UI timing, performance runners, or `qa.config.json` jmeter / lighthouse sections.

## Two surfaces (do not mix)

- **A. Playwright UI performance** — page load, Navigation Timing, resource/network timing on the discovered login page (`tests/e2e/performance/`, `reports/performance/`). Status is **RECORDED**. No SLA is invented. Official CWV scores are not fabricated here.
- **B. JMeter backend/load** — documented API only (`qa.config.json` `urls.api` + `jmeter.path`, JSONPlaceholder GET `/posts`). Not Sauce Demo REST (discovery found 0 XHR on login).

## Source of truth

- Configure load in **`qa.config.json`** → `jmeter` (threads, ramp-up, loop count, path, profile).
- The default profile is **`liveness`**. It records measurements as **RECORDED**, never PASS. `smoke` is an alias of liveness.
- Threshold keys (`jmeter.thresholds.maxP95Ms`, `jmeter.thresholds.maxErrorRatePercent`) may be null. Do not invent numeric SLAs.
- Core Web Vitals live in **`qa.config.json`** → `lighthouse` and `reports/lighthouse/`. If the Lighthouse CLI is missing, record **NOT_EXECUTED** — do not invent scores.
- Playwright UI timings live in `reports/performance/`. Do not merge them into JMeter findings.
- Run **`npm run qa:sync`** to regenerate `tests/performance/jmeter/{smoke,load,stress,spike,soak}/documented-api.jmx` and the liveness alias `tests/performance/load-test.jmx`.
- Prefer editing config + sync over manual JMX-only changes.

## Authorization

- `npm run test:performance` runs **only** the safe liveness/smoke JMeter profile plus Playwright UI timing and Lighthouse.
- Heavy profiles (`load` / `stress` / `spike` / `soak`) require `--authorize-heavy` or `QA_PERF_AUTHORIZE`, plus `allowHeavyAgainst` when that list is non-empty.
- Dedicated pipelines: `.github/workflows/qa-performance-heavy.yml` (`workflow_dispatch` with `authorize-heavy`, optional weekly schedule + `QA_PERF_AUTHORIZE_SCHEDULE`; never `pull_request`) and `jenkins/Jenkinsfile.performance` (`AUTHORIZE_HEAVY` default false). Never authorize heavy on the PR Jenkinsfile.
- Never run heavy/destructive load against production by default.

## Performance considerations

Before raising load, assess:

- **Target environment** — never load-test production without explicit approval.
- **Thread count & ramp-up** — start conservative; increase incrementally.
- **Assertions** — response code, response time thresholds, error rate limits.
- **Side effects** — read-heavy vs write-heavy endpoints; auth/session impact on shared envs.

Document expected baseline (threads, avg response time, error rate) in test comments or `qa.config.json` notes when non-obvious.

## Test types

| Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| **Smoke / liveness** | Small thread count validates the documented API under light concurrency (CI-safe) |
| **Load / stress / spike / soak** | Heavy plans exist as files; they do not auto-run |
| **UI timing** | Single-page Playwright measurement on the login page — not a load test |

## Execution

```bash
npm run test:performance
```

Reports: `reports/jmeter/results.jtl`, `reports/jmeter/html/index.html`, `reports/performance/`, `reports/lighthouse/`.

## Failure triage

- **Product/infra defect**: sustained high latency, 5xx, timeouts under expected load.
- **Automation defect**: wrong host/path, JMeter not installed, malformed JMX — fix config or runner.
- Never hide failures by removing listeners or assertions to make a run pass.

Keep plans **CI/CD-ready** — non-GUI mode, deterministic paths, no local-only hardcoded directories.
